correctness.rationale: For each edge \(e\) with \(d_e\) descendant leaves, \(\Pr(Y_e=1)=1-q^{d_e}\); disjoint clades are independent and a nested pair has covariance \(q^{d_e}(1-q^{d_f})\). These formulas yield the exact integer-polynomial signatures. Canonical unordered full-binary recursion exhausts every shape through sixteen leaves (10,905 shapes at sixteen), finding exactly one two-member collision class at sixteen and none below. An independent exact enumeration of \(2^{16}\) survivor subsets and a separate raw-third-moment recurrence verify the explicit witness. The algebraic identity \(P_A-P_B=q^{2s}z(1-z)(F_U-F_V)^2\) proves mean/variance agreement for every \(q\); the four-leaf inputs give third-moment difference \(-6q^{12}(1-q)^2\), nonzero for \(0<q<1\). A root-grafting argument proves all larger sizes. No finite check is extrapolated into an infinite assertion.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general algorithm yielding the moments from a given input tree does not logically imply sharp uniqueness/non-uniqueness when two input trees are unknown. A normal limit concerns distributions for large tree sequences and does not rule out their finite non-Gaussian third-moment differences. Fixed-count rarefaction is not the common-independent-extinction law.

Nipperess–Matsen (2013) is fixed-count rarefaction, not homogeneous independent extinction. value.rationale: Future phylogenetic diversity is routinely summarized by expectation and variance, including for normal approximations. The theorem determines the first structural limitation of using these full parameter-response curves to identify distributions, and separates an exact risk-event probability by \(q^{14}(1-q)^2\). A universal subtree-grouping identity explains the mechanism, while the unique smallest pair supplies a complete naturally bounded classification. Absolute probability gaps for this witness can be small; no empirical impact is claimed.
